headline: Mattress Firm consolidation drives swing to profitability
summary_short: Somnigroup (formerly Tempur Sealy) posted Q1 2026 net sales of $1,801.5M, up 12.3% y/y, and swung to net income of $104.2M ($0.49 diluted EPS) from a $33.1M loss a year earlier, as the Mattress Firm acquisition was consolidated for a full quarter versus a partial-quarter stub in Q1 2025.
summary_long: Revenue growth was mostly a Mattress Firm comparison effect: its segment sales rose 49.2% on a full quarter of consolidation, while Tempur Sealy North America sales fell 20.2% on intercompany-elimination accounting. Gross margin expanded 690bp to 43.1%, on North America synergies (+620bp) and no repeat of $95.4M in one-time Mattress Firm charges booked in Q1 2025. Operating income rose to $187.1M from $13.2M. Operating cash flow rose $140.1M to $246.5M; capex rose to $60.5M, with FY2026 capex now guided to ~$225M and target leverage guided to 2.0–3.0x (vs 3.07x TTM). Cash fell to $110.8M on debt repayment. Post-quarter, the company agreed to acquire Leggett & Platt in an all-stock deal (~$2.5B), announced April 13, 2026.

drivers.explanation: Growth was driven by including a full quarter of Mattress Firm sales, versus only a stub period in Q1 2025; Tempur Sealy International also grew on strong regional performance.
Gross margin improved 690bp on Tempur Sealy North America synergies and elimination of intercompany Mattress Firm sales, plus no repeat of prior-year one-time acquisition accounting charges.
Gain reflects the inclusion of Mattress Firm and realized sales and cost synergies across segments, partly offset by higher Mattress Firm operating expenses from full-quarter inclusion.
Swing to profit driven by the operating income gain plus a lower effective tax rate (24.3% vs 33.5%), partly offset by continued interest expense on acquisition debt.
Increase was primarily driven by strong operational performance across all segments.
Cash declined as the company made net debt repayments of $134.4 million during the quarter.
The year-over-year swing to profitability is a comparison effect: Q1 2025 carried a partial Mattress Firm quarter plus one-time acquisition costs, neither of which recurred in Q1 2026.
